newsitem.title: USA: US Senate panel approves Pena for energy secretary.
newsitem.headline: US Senate panel approves Pena for energy secretary.

text.p: The Senate Energy Committee on Thursday approved Federico Pena to be the next U.S. energy secretary, sending his name to the full Senate for confirmation.

Pena's nomination had stalled as Alaska Republican Frank Murkowski, the committee chairman, delayed the panel's vote because he said the White House was balking on its responsibilty to find a way to store radioactive waste from utilities' nuclear power reactors.
"The main issue is and has been whether the new secretary will have authority to work with Congress on the nuclear waste problem," Murkowski said before the panel voted 19-0.
After meetings with White House Chief of Staff Erskine Bowles, Murkowski said he felt the administration was more willing to discuss the issue.

Pena, transportation secretary in Clinton's first term, became snared in a fight over where to put spent nuclear fuel from commercial reactors that the federal government legally becomes responsible for next year.

The government is evaluating whether to put a permanent dump at Nevada's Yucca Mountain, but it would be 15 or more years before that site is ready to accept the waste now scattered at some 80 locations across the country.
Running out of storage space and facing local oppostion, utilities are suing the federal government to take the waste on time, which could require a temporary storage measure.
Before Pena's approval vote, Murkowski also said he scheduled a committee vote for next Wednesday on his bill to build a temporary dump in Nevada.

The Senate passed the bill last year, but President Bill Clinton killed it with a veto threat. The White House said the bill would divert resources from building a permanent dump and prejudge Nevada as the ultimate dump site.
